caption: A man exhales on a frosty morning, and his breath appears as a white cloud that drifts away and fades.

sa.check: A person stands outdoors on a cold morning.
A white cloud of breath appears in front of the mouth.
The setting reads as frosty: frost, bare trees or winter clothing.
The cloud appears with the exhale, not between breaths.

pc.expect: Each cloud appears at the exhale, spreads and fades and does not come back, and nothing shows between breaths.
pc.fail: A cloud appears while the chest is drawing in and no breath is going out; or a faded cloud thickens again with no new breath; or a cloud hangs unchanged for the rest of the clip; or the cloud runs back into the mouth.

pc.expect: The cloud starts just in front of the mouth and goes by thinning away.
pc.fail: A cloud appears in the air away from the face with nothing coming from the mouth; or the cloud vanishes in a single frame while still thick; or two clouds appear from one exhale in different places; or the cloud splits into solid pieces.

pc.expect: The cloud drifts and spreads as it thins; it does not fall as a liquid.
pc.fail: The cloud sinks to the ground and pools; or falls in a stream from the mouth; or hangs as a fixed shape without drifting; or pours downward over the chest.

pc.expect: The cloud is a soft haze that spreads, waves and fades; it holds no edges and does not turn solid.
pc.fail: The cloud holds a fixed rigid shape; or turns into solid lumps; or pours like a liquid; or keeps a sharp outline as it drifts.

pc.expect: One person with the same face and clothing; the cloud stays outside the body.
pc.fail: The face changes shape; or a second head appears; or the cloud passes into the chest and out the back; or the clothing turns into another garment.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The clothing, the background and the light stay the same.
pc.fail: The clothing changes colour; or the background changes between frames; or the scene changes from frosty to green.

note: The person is kept because the breath is the caption's subject; the face and expression are not judged.
